title: Line Four, You're Through
gist_ar: برنامج مباشر بمداخلات هاتفية. المذيع بيقاطع، والمتحدثين بيغيّروا موقفهم في نص الكلام.

before_listening.en: Live radio. The host cuts in, the callers change position mid-sentence, and one caller is not arguing what he thinks he's arguing.
before_listening.ar: راديو مباشر. المذيع بيقاطع، والمتصلين بيغيّروا موقفهم وسط الكلام، وواحد منهم بيحتجّ على حاجة تانية خالص.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Eighteen minutes past. We're on the parking scheme, the lines are jammed, and I'll be honest with you, about nine in ten of you are against it. Line four, Mahmoud in Dokki, you're through.

segments.speaker: Mahmoud
segments.text: Yes, morning. Now I've read the consultation document, all sixty pages of it, which I'd wager is more than the councillor who's coming on after me—

segments.speaker: Mahmoud
segments.text: Good, I hope she is. My objection is this. They say the scheme is revenue-neutral. Now, revenue-neutral over what period? Because if you read annex C, the capital cost of the barriers is amortised over twelve years and the income projection runs for seven. You cannot call that neutral. You can call it neutral for seven years and then a bill.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That's a specific point and I'll put it to her. But can I ask you — if she came back and said 'you're right, we'll amortise it over seven', would you then support the scheme?

segments.speaker: Mahmoud
segments.text: ...I'd have to look at the— no. No, I wouldn't.

segments.speaker: Mahmoud
segments.text: It isn't only the accounting. It's that nobody asked us and now they're asking us about the numbers so that the answer has to be about numbers.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Right. Thank you, that's a much better argument than the one you started with. Line two, Fatima, you're a resident of the same street I think?

segments.speaker: Fatima
segments.text: I am, and I'll say something unpopular. I'm for it. And the reason I'm for it isn't the traffic, it's that I've got a mother who's eighty-one and a wheelchair that needs a metre and a half of clearance to get out of the car, and at the moment I have that clearance roughly one morning in five.

segments.speaker: Fatima
segments.text: Under the scheme there's a marked bay outside number forty. Which I would have. Now — I want to be fair to Mahmoud, because he's my neighbour and he's not wrong about the consultation. Nobody knocked on my door either. I found out from a lamp post. But I'd rather be presented with a bad process and a bay than a good process and no bay, and I think a lot of people who feel like me aren't ringing you, because it sounds like you're admitting you'll take anything.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That's — hold on, that's the most interesting thing anybody's said this morning. Say that last bit again.

segments.speaker: Fatima
segments.text: If you say out loud that you'll accept a scheme that was pushed through badly, you sound like somebody who can be pushed. So people like me stay quiet, and then the phone-in tells you nine in ten are against, and the nine in ten is real but it isn't everybody.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Councillor, you've been listening. You've got ninety seconds after this.

gist_question.q: What does Fatima suggest about the 'nine in ten against' figure?
options: That the station has simply miscounted the calls it received this morning
That it is genuine but under-represents supporters who stay silent
That most callers do not live on the affected street
That opponents are ringing in more than once

questions.q: What does the host expose about Mahmoud's position?
options: That he would oppose the scheme even if his accounting objection were fixed
That he has not in fact read the sixty-page consultation document he claims to cite
That he is speaking on the councillor's behalf
That his figures come from annex D, not annex C

questions.q: What is Mahmoud's technical objection to 'revenue-neutral'?
options: The barriers cost more than the document states
The cost is spread over twelve years but income is only projected for seven
The scheme has no income projection at all
Neutrality is measured per street rather than per district

questions.q: Why is Fatima in favour of the scheme?
options: Because it will reduce traffic on her street
Because a marked bay outside number forty would give her the wheelchair clearance she needs
Because the consultation process was properly run
Because she disagrees with her neighbour on principle

questions.q: What does Mahmoud finally say his real objection is?
options: That residents were never asked, and the numbers debate is a way of forcing the answer onto numbers
That the councillor has not read the document
That the barriers will be installed outside his home
That seven years is too short a period
